name: Apache Software Foundation
body: Preloaded HSTS, a security.txt, a content security policy, and Core Web Vitals that pass for real visitors. But none of the 20 pages read, the home page included, has a meta description.
lesson: Give each page a description of about 150 characters. Search and AI answers quote it when they introduce you.
summary: www.apache.org scores 74 out of 100 (C). 2 checks fail now, 23 are at risk, and 18 pass. Fix first: 2 form controls have no label.

fix.title: 2 form controls have no label
fix.evidence: On /foundation/press/kit/, /logos/. Screen readers announce them as an unnamed field.
fix.fix: Pair each control with <label for>, wrap it in a label, or add aria-label.

fix.title: Links carry email addresses in the URL
fix.evidence: 1 link on /dev/ put an email address in the query string. Analytics tools record full URLs, and Google's terms forbid sending personal data.
fix.fix: Move the email out of the URL (POST it, or use an opaque token).

fix.title: 44 images have no alt attribute
fix.fix: Describe informative images. Give decorative ones alt="".

fix.title: 20 pages have no meta description
fix.evidence: /, /foundation/policies/conduct, /community-resources/, /foundation/buy_stuff and 16 more. Google and AI answers then write their own snippet from whatever text they find.
fix.fix: Write a 50 to 160 character description for each page that says what a reader gets.

fix.title: 20 pages have no canonical link
fix.evidence: /, /foundation/policies/conduct, /community-resources/, /foundation/buy_stuff and 16 more. Without it, tracking parameters and trailing slashes can split ranking signals.
fix.fix: Add <link rel="canonical" href="…"> with the page's own https URL.

fix.title: X-Content-Type-Options is not sent
fix.evidence: Browsers may guess a file's type and run it as script. Missing on all 20 pages read.

works.title: Every internal link that was opened answered
AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page
Plain http redirects permanently to https
